chapter: Guitarists and the Pierron and Brown bands
title: Piron's band: Lorenzo Tio, Cottrell and the banjoists
summary: Piron's band read arrangements but took hot breaks, led by Lorenzo Tio. Souchon corrects an earlier statement about Steve Lewis and recalls drummer Cottrell's moving eyebrows. He and Russell try to name the banjoist.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yes, a regular set thing. And he was terrific. They gave him stuff on the violin, breaks to do on that, and featured his singing and everything else. That's when they had very much larger group. They grew up to about a ten-piece band. The other guitarists around New Orleans proper were none that I know of except the McKay brothers, which were both white, and then all the Negro bands. And they all, as I say, I don't remember a banjo until much later when Johnny St. Cyr began using that six-string. Now, the... And they didn't use a piano if the guitar was there, and vice versa. They didn't use a guitar if the piano was there. Very seldom you'd have them both. And at the Tulane Gym, they never had any piano. Now, coming back to the Pierron band, I made a mistake in a statement I made a long time ago, and that was corrected by Mrs. Pierron. Steve Lewis, who played with Pierron, never did play with Oliver, although even Pierron led Oliver's band for many years on the violin up at the gym and all around town. And they used to practice music in his little barber shop, which was not far away from Big 25. Now, Pierron's band were also readers, and they used arrangements, but they did a great deal of takeoff. And the best one, of course, was Lorenzo Teo. I enjoyed Cottrell Sr. on drums very much. He was a big, tall, very black, but very well-chiseled features, and he had white, white hair, and he was a good dresser. But he had an extraordinary characteristic. His eyebrows would go up with every beat of the drum. He'd just look up. He'd move. His whole scalp would go up with every beat. On the offbeat, too. Always. Really? Yeah. Now, Pierron had a banjo with him as a rule, which was either, what's his name the trumpet players?
Charlie Bokaj, what's the name of this other little short fellow?
Oh, Simon. Not Simon. John Marrero.
Wait. I have his picture, and I'm going to pull that out for you later on. No, wait a minute.
No, it wouldn't be Marrero. Anyway, I think it's on the picture.
We have some of those pictures, too. Yeah, there's two different. That's right. I think it was John Marrero was with him, too.
